evals.prompt: In an established app, move one existing Save button 8px lower and keep it consistent with the current component library. Explain the implementation approach only. The project already has DESIGN.md and tokens.
evals.expected_output: A proportionate small-change workflow using the existing contract without unnecessary system bootstrap.
expectations: Treats this as a small change and does not create or rewrite the full design system.
Uses the existing button component and spacing tokens rather than adding an ad-hoc value.
Checks representative sibling instances before changing a shared rule.
Requires rendered verification of the changed control in context.

evals.prompt: Design a new settings page for an existing dark-teal product. It has profile fields, notification toggles, integrations, Save, Disconnect, and Delete account. Describe the design contract and hierarchy before code.
evals.expected_output: A coherent pre-build contract covering task hierarchy, palette roles, surfaces, danger separation, tokens, and review handoff.
expectations: Makes Save the dominant decision action while toggles, chevrons, and row actions remain subordinate.
Separates destructive actions into a clearly bounded danger area.
Defines non-neutral color roles and surface separation against actual grounds.
Uses existing tokens/validator and includes grayscale or squint hierarchy verification before build completion.

evals.prompt: Choose a visual direction for a Japanese mobile journaling app. The brief asks for dark mode, glassmorphism, cards, asymmetry, retro details, and responsive design. Explain the direction before code.
evals.expected_output: A coherent direction that separates visual language, layout, primitives, modes, effects, and requirements instead of mixing every requested term.
expectations: Classifies dark mode as a mode, cards as a content primitive, asymmetry as layout, glass as an effect, and responsive behavior as a requirement.
Commits one dominant visual language and explicitly excludes incompatible or unsupported treatments.
Justifies the direction from task, platform, content, audience, and brand evidence rather than an industry stereotype.
Checks the direction against dense, narrow, localized, error, empty, and reduced-motion conditions.

evals.prompt: Design an Android tablet and phone inventory app using Material 3 Expressive. Describe the system and adaptive behavior before implementation.
evals.expected_output: A Material-native plan grounded in tokens, component behavior, states, adaptive structure, and controlled expressiveness.
expectations: Declares the Material adoption boundary and verifies the current library/component guidance.
Maps reference, system-role, and component tokens without creating a competing token source.
Defines compact and expanded structural/navigation behavior from the inventory task rather than only resizing.
Uses expressive shape, type, color, and motion selectively and rechecks hierarchy, accessibility, states, and reduced motion.

evals.prompt: Add an AI feature to our expense tool: automatically categorise each uploaded receipt into one of our twelve expense categories and submit it. Design it.
evals.expected_output: Step 1 answered with the decision contract, the AI value gate run before the interaction is designed, and autonomy placed on the spectrum rather than set to automatic.
expectations: Answers the three decision-contract questions concretely — a user outcome, a named trade-off stated as 'we accept X to get Y', and what stays under direct human control.

Runs the does-AI-add-value gate before designing the flow, and notes that categorisation against twelve fixed categories has a largely deterministic version — rules on merchant and amount — that would be right more often.
Flags that submission is the consequential half and treats it separately from categorisation rather than designing one automatic feature.
Places the feature on the autonomy spectrum with a reason, and does not put automatic submission past 'Acts with approval'; treats spend and irreversibility as the ceiling.
Says the autonomy level is earned and moves one step at a time, rather than offering a single on/off automation switch.
Does not skip Step 1 and go straight to layout, and does not treat 'it is an AI feature' as the justification for using a model.

evals.prompt: Design the main screen for a bilingual English/Japanese incident console with a dense alert table, a persistent filter bar, loading/empty/error/stale states, long service names, and a destructive bulk Resolve action. Describe the visual and interaction contract before code.
evals.expected_output: A visual contract stress-tested against density, localization, all non-default states, persistent retrieval controls and consequential bulk action.
expectations: Defines hierarchy for filters, alert data, row actions and the consequential bulk action rather than giving every control equal prominence.
Designs loading, empty, error and stale states as different information and recovery needs.
Tests Japanese/English labels and long service names without relying on truncation for the primary decision information.
Keeps filters and selected state structurally usable at narrow widths and hands URL ownership to the IA contract where appropriate.
Separates the destructive bulk action, scopes its target set clearly, and specifies confirmation or undo based on consequence and reversibility.
Requires representative rendered evidence for dense, narrow, localized and failure conditions rather than validating only the happy state.

evals.prompt: Design a mobile 'who is free now' roster. Some people have available, busy, away, offline, or expiring statuses; most records have no presence data. The visual direction proposes green/red/grey avatar treatments. Describe the status model, component behaviour, accessibility, and what the roster should announce.
evals.expected_output: A presence design that separates missing data from real states, uses a second non-colour and programmatic channel, treats contrast scope carefully, and avoids narrating ambient roster churn.
expectations: Does not coerce missing presence data into available, offline, unknown, or another asserted state; absence renders no indicator unless the product defines a meaningful unknown state.
Requires meaningful presence to survive hue, greying, desaturation, or opacity through a persistent non-colour channel and an accessible name or adjacent programmatic label.
Does not claim that every decorative status dot automatically fails WCAG at 3:1; it verifies the current 1.4.11 scope before citing it.
Defines the state vocabulary and precedence as a product decision rather than importing a universal set.
Keeps ambient updates quiet by default and announces only changes timely and relevant to the active task.
Treats expiry by disappearance as a cautious default, and makes a boundary label or countdown an explicit project decision when remaining time changes the user's decision.

evals.prompt: Design a mobile home screen with a horizontally scrolling set of six personally relevant cards above bottom navigation and a persistent mini-player. The proposal asks for a 48dp next-card peek, edge-to-edge swiping, mandatory snap, and custom pointer dragging. Explain the layout and interaction contract before code.
evals.expected_output: A rail and bottom-stack decision that distinguishes guidance from standards, avoids invented thresholds, preserves native input and focus behaviour, and respects platform gesture zones.
expectations: Tests whether users have a reason to seek later items and treats the rail as a decision rather than a universal carousel ban or default.
Rejects 48dp as a universal best-practice peek threshold and states that no authoritative peek amount or item-count ceiling exists.
Prefers native overflow when suitable; if custom dragging replaces it, requires a single-pointer previous/next alternative under WCAG 2.5.7.
Keeps the rail keyboard reachable, does not aria-hide merely off-screen native items, and verifies mandatory snap with logical scroll padding and visible focus.
Uses a gutter rather than broad Android gesture exclusions and states that the bottom home/quick-switch area cannot be excluded; scopes 200dp to side back-gesture exclusions.

Makes bottom navigation primary and the mini-player subordinate, with collapse/minimise behaviour considered, without inventing a fixed-chrome height budget or claiming stacking is categorically forbidden.
